name: Ikhin

Open Science Repository Language and Linguistics, Online (open-access), e70081942. doi:10.7392/Research.70081942 (CC-BY 3.0; author's note 1: drawn from chapter 6 of his 2010 University of Ibadan PhD thesis 'A phonology of Ikhin').
catalog_locator: Unpaginated online article. Quote 1: section 2 'The typology of the tone system of Ikhin', first paragraph (saved plain). Quote 2: last paragraph of section 6 before 'Conclusion' (line 69). Quote 3: 'Conclusion', first sentence (line 71).
catalog_quote: Ikhin is a terraced level tone system with two basic tones, high and low. Perceptual analysis suggests that there are two tones; High and Low but sometimes there seems to be some kind of low tone raising in citation form. However, in a construction where an apparent mid relates to other tones they are clearly seen as low. The following are the minimal pairs of words differentiated only by tonal contrast. ... All these examples are a clear evidence of the fact that Ikhin has two basic tones, High and Low. The language exploits these two basic tones to make lexical and syntactic contrasts as shown in the earlier examples. ... Following the instrumental phonetic facts given so far, there is no doubt that Ikhin is a terraced level tone system: it has two tones; it has downdrift that affects successive lows where a low tone is realised at a lower level than the immediately preceding low; and it has downstepped high (!H).
world_status: statement found in an open source

new_statements.rule_in_words: Ikhin is a two-tone (H/L) terraced-level register tone language with non-phonemic downstep, downdrift and word-final downglide of L; every syllable (CV or V) carries a lexical tone. No source opened says anything about word stress or accent, positive or negative; no stress rule is stated.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Not mentioned in any opened source.
new_statements.exceptions: None about stress. On tone: disyllabic nouns show three patterns, trisyllabic nouns six (LLL, LLH, LHL, HLH, HLL, HHL); verbs and numerals are L-toned in citation form except /eha/ 'six' (LH); personal pronouns H in citation form; low-tone raising perceived in citation forms is analysed as L.
new_statements.domain_note: Lexical (word-level) tone with instrumental F0 evidence on citation forms and short constructions; tone phrase is the domain for downdrift/downstep.
new_statements.identity_note: All opened sources describe 'Ikhin' as spoken at Ikhin town, Owan East LGA, Edo State (c. 30,000 speakers; data from seven speakers in Ikhin town plus one in Ibadan). The Glottolog languoid ikhi1234 is Ikhin-Arokho [ikh]; the Arokho (Aokho) variety is not described in any opened source (it is only listed in the unopened Lewis 2013 and Decker et al. 2024 records). No separate glottocode for Arokho at language level.

sources.locator: Unpaginated online article: section 2 'The typology of the tone system of Ikhin' (first quote) and 'Conclusion' (second quote)
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. Whole paper is on tone: 'Ikhin is a terraced level tone system with two basic tones, high and low' (sec. 2), plus non-phonemic downstep, downdrift, downglide of final L; lexical tone patterns for nouns (LL/LH/HL etc.), verbs L in citation form, pronouns H in citation form; instrumental F0 evidence. No word 'stress' or 'accent' anywhere in the text.

sources.citation: Oladimeji, Olaide A. & Opoola, Bolanle T. 2021. Ikhin Tone and Nasality: Autosegmental Effects. Journal of Language Teaching and Research 12(4): 603-610. doi:10.17507/jltr.1204.11
sources.note: 'Ikhin is a tone language.' (p. 605); 'Ikhin has low, high, and contour tones, for example (The language also has downdrift, downstep and downglide).' (p. 605). The only occurrence of 'stress' (p. 604) is a generic remark about autosegmental theory ('Tone, nasality, stress and length phonology are not well-suited to rules..'), not about Ikhin.

sources.citation: Oladimeji, Olaide A. 2022. Grammatical tone: H tomorph, a marker of attribution in Ikhin, an Edoid language. European Journal of Applied Linguistics Studies 5(1): 186-196. doi:10.46827/ejals.v5i1.359
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Abstract (p. 186): 'The typology of Ikhin tone system is "two tones plus a downstep"'; paper is on the H tomorph marking attributive constructions and L tomorph in downstep.

sources.citation: Oladimeji, Olaide. 2022. A constraint-based analysis of the syllable structure of Ikhin. European Journal of Applied Linguistics Studies 5(2). doi:10.46827/ejals.v5i2.365
sources.note: Nothing on stress. 'Ikhin is a tone language and tone is seen as a fundamental unit that defines a syllable.' (p. 5); phonemic syllable types CV and V, surface CCV via glide formation, no syllabic nasal.

sources.citation: Oladimeji, Olaide A. & Opoola, Bolanle T. 2021. Noun Class System in Ikhin, an Edoid Language. Journal of Language Teaching and Research 12(5). doi:10.17507/jltr.1205.18
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Literature note (sec. III): Folarin 1982 'dwells mainly on the Phonetics of the language.. the identification of two basic tones, high /H/ and low /L/'.

sources.citation: Opoola, Bolanle T. & Oladimeji, Olaide. 2021. Vowel Elision in Ikhin, an Edoid Language in South-south Nigeria. Journal of Language Teaching and Research 12(3): 352-361. doi:10.17507/jltr.1203.04
sources.note: Nothing on stress. Treats vowel elision, glide formation and tone stability (floating L/H relinking to form contour tones); Ikhin nouns disyllabic V(C)V or trisyllabic.

sources.citation: Oladimeji, Olaide. 2023. Tense, Aspect and Negation in Ikhin: The Role of Tone. International Journal of Social Science Humanity & Management Research 2(01): 01-16. (open deposit: Zenodo, doi:10.5281/zenodo.7503395, CC-BY-4.0)
sources.note: Examines the realization of tone on verbal elements (tense, progressive aspect, negation, verb stem); 'This language has two basic tones and a downstep. Verb stems in Ikhin do not have tonal representation in the lexicon.
